author: Codex blind first-pass assessor

source_artifacts.claim: The room defines the BUBBLES hold, RESCUE latch, gates, no hazards, optional collectibles, exits, and Gem bubble configuration.
Bubble hits float Isp or stick Pac; the effect durations are defined.
The Gem attack starts when BUBBLES is active and follows a windup/cooldown cycle.
A falling Pac landing on top of a bubble bounces; otherwise bubble hits apply float/sticky effects.
Hold and latch pad states control barriers; latch effects persist.
Isp/Pac use separate movement and jump keys.

prior_knowledge.concept: Gem bubbles previously introduced distinct effects: Isp float and Pac top bounce, with side contact sticking Pac. Here Pac starts the bubble attack and holds the trigger while Isp uses float to reach RESCUE; Pac does not need a bubble bounce on the mandatory route.

evidence.claim: The earlier room visibly introduces bubble-role text for Isp and Pac.
Earlier campaign instructions present bubble roles and both-exit control objective.

prior_knowledge.concept: Character-specific hold/latch pads and gate-opening effects have appeared earlier (including levels 08 and 12); this room combines Pac’s hold to enable Gem’s bubble with Isp’s rescue latch.

evidence.claim: Position 7 uses character-specific steady and rescue pads to open routes.

mechanics.fact: Pac must occupy BUBBLES to start Gem’s recurring bubble attack. The attack has a 0.8-second windup and 1.5-second cooldown; a bubble hitting Isp applies FLOAT for 1.4 seconds, allowing Isp to rise and steer right to RESCUE.

evidence.claim: BUBBLES is Pac-only hold and RESCUE is Isp-only latch opening both gates.
Gem’s bubble attack starts on the BUBBLES pad with 0.8-second windup/1.5-second cooldown and can be interrupted by RESCUE.
Bubble hits give Isp FLOAT and Pac STICKY for defined durations.
The bubble attack is enabled by the active start pad and cycles through cooldown/windup.
With Pac still holding BUBBLES, Isp rises from y464 toward the rescue shelf.

mechanics.fact: RESCUE is an Isp latch. It opens Pac’s entry gate and Isp’s stair gate; once latched, Pac can leave BUBBLES, climb the right steps, and jump left to the matching exits.

evidence.claim: RESCUE latches and opens both player-specific gates; the exits are on the shelf.
Latch state persists after the activating hero leaves and continues applying gate effects.
Isp reaches the matching exit before Pac climbs the right-side route.
The stable level_13 trace completes both exits without deaths.

mechanics.fact: There are no authored hazards; a continuous floor under the route makes a missed lift/fall nonlethal. The two sparks are optional, one for each hero, and the ordinary route does not record their collection.

evidence.claim: The room has a continuous floor, elevated shelf/steps, no hazards, two optional collectibles, and matching exits.
Both exits complete with zero deaths; collectible status is not represented in the attempt summary.

legal_routes.name: Pac holds BUBBLES; Isp floats to RESCUE; Pac climbs steps to exits

steps.goal: Start Gem’s bubbles and keep the attack enabled for Isp.
steps.action: Remain on the BUBBLES pad while Isp moves within bubble range and waits for the recurring projectile.
steps.expected_feedback: Gem begins the automatic bubble attack; Pac’s hold is not a bounce action. The scripted trace leaves Pac stationary while Isp progresses.

evidence.claim: BUBBLES is a Pac-only hold pad.
Pac remains at its starting location while Isp begins moving.

steps.goal: Use the bubble’s FLOAT effect to reach the RESCUE shelf.
steps.action: Move right into Gem’s bubble path; once floated upward, steer right to the RESCUE pad and latch it.
steps.expected_feedback: Bubble contact gives Isp FLOAT; RESCUE opens both gates and interrupts further bubbles. The trace rises to the shelf and reaches Isp’s exit.
steps.observed_feedback: The scripted route shows Isp rising to the rescue shelf and later reaching the exit; effect feedback itself is not separately logged.

evidence.claim: Isp bubble contact applies FLOAT.
RESCUE latches both gates and interrupts Gem’s bubbles.
Isp rises vertically while Pac stays on BUBBLES.
Isp reaches the upper exit after crossing the RESCUE shelf.

steps.goal: Follow through the opened gate and reach the Pac exit.
steps.action: After Isp latches RESCUE, leave BUBBLES, move right to the lower and upper steps, then jump left onto the shelf toward PAC EXIT.
steps.expected_feedback: The rescue latch opens Pac’s route and the two steps permit a climb to the shelf.
steps.observed_feedback: The route moves Pac right through the steps and finishes at PAC EXIT.

evidence.claim: The lower/upper steps lead to the shelf and Pac’s matching exit.
Pac advances right after Isp reaches the exit.
Both exits complete without death.
The correctly attributed stable-ID route completes both matching exits with zero deaths in 10.5417 seconds; this proves scripted feasibility only.

isp: Move into Gem’s bubble path, use FLOAT to reach the shelf, and latch RESCUE to open both gates and stop further bubbles; finish at the upper matching exit.
pac: Hold BUBBLES to activate Gem’s recurring bubble attack; after RESCUE is latched, leave and climb the right-side steps to the lower matching exit.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac leaves BUBBLES before Isp has reached RESCUE.
common_mistakes.consequence: Gem’s bubble attack is no longer enabled, so Isp loses the repeatable float opportunity and may fall back to the floor.
common_mistakes.recovery: Pac can return to BUBBLES; the floor is safe and the attack can restart after its cooldown. This recovery is source-derived, not exercised.

evidence.claim: BUBBLES is a Pac-only hold pad.
Gem’s bubble attack starts while BUBBLES is active.
Continuous floor provides safe lower refuge.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac touches a bubble from the side instead of landing on top.
common_mistakes.consequence: Pac receives STICKY for 0.6 seconds; movement is stopped and jump input is suppressed during the effect.
common_mistakes.recovery: Wait for the short effect to expire, then return to the pad or steps; no death is required by the authored layout.

evidence.claim: Pac bubble contact applies STICKY and clears jump buffer.
A continuous safe floor is present.

common_mistakes.mistake: Isp misses a bubble or falls short of the RESCUE shelf.
common_mistakes.consequence: Isp falls to the safe floor and must regain the bubble route.
common_mistakes.recovery: Pac can keep holding BUBBLES for another recurring shot; timing/recovery is inferred from the repeatable attack and safe floor, not observed as a failure.

evidence.claim: The floor is continuous and BUBBLES remains a repeatable hold trigger.
The attack repeats after cooldown/windup.

optional_collectibles: Isp’s blue spark is near the rescue shelf at (465,280); Pac’s orange spark is on the upper step at (960,330). Neither is required for both exits and the trace does not report pickups.

reasoning.rationale: The puzzle has one clear dependency: Pac holds BUBBLES while Isp uses FLOAT to reach RESCUE; the rescue latch then opens Pac’s route. The canvas names the pad and roles but does not show the specific sequence.

evidence.claim: The source defines the BUBBLES hold and RESCUE latch.
Canvas labels show bubble roles and RESCUE near exits, without showing causal links.
A scripted route confirms this sequence is feasible, not whether novices infer it.

cooperation.rationale: Both heroes have necessary distinct work: Pac sustains the trigger, Isp uses FLOAT and activates RESCUE, then Pac follows the opened route. This is one main handoff rather than repeated simultaneous coordination.

evidence.claim: The two pads are assigned to different heroes and open routes.
Pac begins moving only after Isp has already reached the upper exit area.

execution.rationale: Isp must steer while temporarily floating to a raised shelf; Pac later makes several step jumps to reach the same shelf. The scripted trace succeeds without deaths, but this is not a human error-rate estimate.

evidence.claim: The route includes a raised shelf and two steps.
Isp rises toward the shelf after entering the bubble route.
The route completes without deaths.

timing.rationale: The bubble attack repeats on a 1.5-second cooldown with 0.8-second windup, so Isp must be near its path and use the temporary 1.4-second FLOAT effect. Pac can keep the trigger held and retry; there is no one-shot narrow window.

evidence.claim: The attack has a recurring cooldown and windup and begins from BUBBLES.
FLOAT has a 1.4-second duration.
Scripted clear completes without death; human timing demand remains unmeasured.

hazards.rationale: No hazards are authored, and a continuous floor lies below the bubble route and elevated shelf. The mandatory route does not require exposure to lethal danger.

evidence.claim: A continuous floor, steps, exits, and empty hazards are authored.

novelty.rationale: Bubble roles were introduced earlier at level_08, and character-specific pad/latch roles are familiar. The new combination is using Pac’s hold to start Gem’s bubble so Isp can float to a rescue latch; Pac’s top-bounce behavior is optional to this clear.

evidence.claim: Position 7 presents the same Isp-float/Pac-top-bounce bubble roles.
The current room combines bubble activation with a rescue latch.

recovery_cost.rationale: A missed bubble or sticky side contact delays progress but does not expose players to configured hazards; the lower floor is safe and Pac can continue holding the trigger for later bubbles. No failed route was observed.

evidence.claim: A continuous lower floor and persistent hold trigger are authored.
Pac sticky effect expires after 0.6 seconds.

solution_clarity.rationale: Visible bubble-role text, BUBBLES, and RESCUE labels give a usable starting hypothesis. The player still must discover that Pac’s pad starts the enemy bubble, Isp should take the float, and RESCUE opens Pac’s route.

evidence.claim: Canvas shows START: BUBBLES, bubble roles, RESCUE, and both exits.
The subtitle describes a lift through a grumpy liver without stating the activation/order.

control_friction.rationale: The movement and jump keys are distinct, bubble activation is automatic from Pac’s occupied pad, and the correctly attributed ordinary-input trace completes the room. This does not establish human comfort.

evidence.claim: Isp and Pac have disjoint movement and jump key mappings.
The ordinary-input route completes both exits without deaths.

confidence_reason: Source mechanics, visible labels, and a correctly attributed stable-ID ordinary-input clear establish the route and feasibility. No human interaction, failure, or recovery was observed, so first-time discovery and lived difficulty remain unmeasured.

confirmed: The both-exit objective matches source completion, and the labels correctly identify Pac’s bubble trigger and Isp’s float role.
The idle-only limitation was correctly preserved; no action feedback was witnessed in pass one.
missed_mechanics: Pac’s BUBBLES hold starts Gem’s recurring bubble attack; Pac need not top-bounce to complete the mandatory route.
Isp must receive the bubble’s FLOAT effect and latch RESCUE; that latch opens both gates and interrupts further bubbles.
Pac then climbs the authored steps and jumps left to the matching exit; both optional sparks are separate.
There are no authored hazards and the floor is continuous beneath the route.
incorrect_inferences: The first pass treated Pac’s top bounce as a likely mandatory route action; the stable-ID ordinary route shows Pac remains on BUBBLES until Isp reaches the shelf, then uses steps. This route does not require Pac to bounce on a bubble.
The idle RECHARGING label was correctly not interpreted as witnessed action feedback; source establishes only a recurring automatic cooldown/windup, not a player-triggered recharge.
changed_judgments: Reasoning remains 2: source confirms one hold-to-float-to-latch sequence, not a longer chain of hidden dependencies.
Cooperation remains 2: Pac starts/supports bubbles, Isp rescues, then Pac takes the open route; this is a single major handoff.
Execution remains 2: the source and route confirm a float-controlled shelf approach and step jumps, but the zero-death script does not calibrate human precision.

Timing changes from null to 1 because Pac must hold the trigger while Isp reaches a recurring bubble; 0.8-second windup and repeatable 1.5-second cooldown make this a readable repeatable opportunity, not a narrow window.
Hazards change from null to 0 because the authored level has no hazard objects and a continuous lower floor; geometry alone did not establish danger in pass one.
Novelty remains 2: bubble roles and pads were previously introduced, while using a held trigger to route Isp into a rescue latch is a new combination.
Recovery changes from null to 1 because Pac can keep the trigger active and missed bubbles return players to safe floor; this is source-derived, not an observed mistake recovery.
Solution clarity remains 2: the visible labels suggest the actors and objects but do not explicitly map BUBBLES to Gem’s attack or RESCUE to Pac’s gate.
Control friction changes from null to 0 from distinct mappings, automatic pad activation, and a successful ordinary-input route; no human comfort was measured.
unresolved: No human first-encounter route or mistake recovery was observed.
The attempt summary records positions/status, not explicit bubble-contact events or pad feedback; sequence interpretation combines source with route positions.
Optional collectible pickup actions are not represented in the attempt.

single_operator_note: A single operator would switch between Isp and Pac keys while keeping Pac on BUBBLES until Isp latches RESCUE; simultaneous control is not required by the recorded route. No one-operator comfort was measured.
